paras: The lynching of two Black men at Camden, Arkansas, took place in or before late July 1895, when a mob overpowered the sheriff, took out two prisoners and hanged them. The men, who were not named, were said to have murdered a white man. The episode survives only as a one-sentence wire brief reprinted in small Northern Plains weeklies.

According to the brief, the two men were in the sheriff's hands at Camden when a mob overpowered him. The mob "took out and hanged two negroes who had murdered a white man." The item gives no date, no names for the prisoners, the sheriff or the dead white man, and no size or description of the mob.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The brief ran under the heading "Criminal Doings" in the Pioneer Press of Miller, South Dakota, and the Pierre Weekly Free Press on August 1, 1895. The Pioneer Express of North Dakota printed it the next day, and the Bottineau Courant repeated it on August 10, each time word for word. In every copy the item sat among unrelated shootings, stabbings and trials, and it stated the prisoners' guilt as fact without comment on the mob.
No coverage in the Black press was found for August or September 1895.

reader.title: Lynching of two Black men at Camden, Arkansas (1895)
bases: The only report says a mob overpowered the sheriff at Camden, Ark., took out two Black prisoners and hanged them [A1].

A 'mob' overpowered the sheriff and hanged two men accused of murdering a white man, so two people were killed without lawful authority by a group acting in the name of punishing a crime [A1]; the account rests on one syndicated brief.
Every copy found carries the same one-sentence wire brief word for word [A1, A2, A3, A5], so there is one source and no independent or local report.
